Subject: HelixChain urgent: p99 spike + 5xx surge — need quick containment + exec update

Team — HelixChain (big checkout flow) reports a P99 latency jump and increased 5xx starting ~08:40 PT. They attached traces and a kv-cache stats CSV. Customer-facing notes below:
- Impact: user checkouts are timing out; visible in production dashboards and on their side.
- Scope: multi-endpoint but their traces show many requests piling up behind a small set of workers; suspect KV cache thrash + concurrency caps.

Immediate asks:
1) Karthik: please triage and propose a short-lived mitigation (bump concurrency cap, offload long-running requests to lower-latency model, or enable cache bypass) — need a safe plan we can tell the customer.
2) Ben: prep a one-paragraph customer-facing status we can send in 20 min.
3) Marissa/Hannah: heads-up for potential exec escalation if mitigation doesn't restore service in 1h.

Attaching HelixChain traces (they sent p99_trace_excerpt.txt and kvcache-stats-20261001.csv).

Thanks —
Jasmine

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: HelixChain urgent: p99 spike + 5xx surge — triage notes and mitigations

Quick triage summary (results from 10:12–11:20):
- Root cause hypothesis: rapid fan-in of many short requests caused KV cache eviction storms on the worker pool serving HelixChain traffic. Evictions increased backend recompute and caused request queueing; when queues hit concurrency cap X, requests started to be rejected (5xx) or timed out at the application layer, producing the p99 spike.
- Evidence: their kvcache-stats CSV shows several cache shards with eviction rates 6–8x baseline. Traces show long blocking times waiting on KV warm-up for identical prefixes.

Immediate mitigations executed (11:00–11:30):
1) Temporarily raised per-customer concurrency cap by 30% for HelixChain on the affected pool (safest rollout rule: padding + rate limit).
2) Enabled short-term aggressive prefix caching (preserve hot keys for 10m) to reduce cache churn.
3) Added a model-fallback route for requests with >3k tokens to go to the lower-latency quantized variant (no change to customer model version).

Customer impact: p99 dropped ~40% in first 15 minutes and 5xxs reduced markedly in our telemetry. We are still seeing intermittent longer tails on a small subset of requests (those with very long context and large KV warmups).

Next actions (owner):
- Karthik: continue monitoring; collect full heap/profile samples and KV hot-key list (I pulled a sample and attached heapdump-sample.zip).
- Ben: send the customer-facing update with mitigation summary and ETA for full root-cause.
- Marissa/Hannah: recommend we prepare an exec update if we can't fully stabilize in the next 60–90m.

Notes on risk: raising concurrency cap increases resource consumption; if traffic continues to spike we may need to throttle non-critical routes.

--
Karthik Iyer
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Sofia — quick status update from Redwood: thanks for the traces. Our SRE team identified cache-eviction storms causing queueing and implemented an emergency mitigations set (temporary concurrency padding + prefix-caching + model fallback for very long sessions). Early telemetry shows a notable reduction in both p99 latency and 5xx errors.

What we're doing next:
- Continued monitoring (Karthik) and deep collection of traces and heap profiles for a full RCA.
- We'll share a preliminary RCA within 8 business hours and a full postmortem within 72 hours.

If you can, please indicate whether HelixChain wants us to: 1) keep the concurrency bump in place for 24 hours, or 2) revert after we confirm stabilization. We recommend keeping it for a short window while we finish the RCA to avoid relapse.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this is customer-critical. We'll stay on this until it's fully resolved.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
